summary: The milestone's 13 compute-bound completions occupied 172.5 minutes. Optimization should start with the 70.92- and 69.26-minute entries; neither their expensive stages nor an accelerator fault are demonstrated, and the locked compute-task idle field is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Elapsed work is concentrated in the 70.92- and 69.26-minute compute-bound entries, while missing stage spans leave the cause of each long path unknown.
The clock source fell back to disk modification times because the live git-log path found zero commits, obscuring waits, overlap, and the actual critical path.
The accelerator sample has no experiment or compute-stage correlation, so it cannot establish whole-task device efficiency; the locked classification records no accelerator-efficiency fault.
Launch cardinality and dispatch choice were not captured, leaving no basis to identify a two-or-more-model launch that should have used the dual-GPU runner.
improvements_suggested: Give every experiment durable stage spans for preparation, queueing, inference, and finalization instead of deriving elapsed time from commits or file timestamps.
Attach experiment and stage identifiers to timestamped device utilization, memory, and process samples; evaluate zero utilization only during a declared compute span.
Persist model cardinality, dispatch implementation, device assignment, and fallback cause at launch, selecting the dual-GPU runner only when at least two models execute concurrently.
Let the queue place independent one-model jobs on separate devices when both are runnable, without changing the correct single-device semantics of each job.
Insert resumable boundaries and stage budgets into the two longest paths to expose repeated initialization, waiting, or inference.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Enable two-device queue placement for independent one-model runs.
Correlate durable stage spans with process-level accelerator telemetry.
Add resume points and stage budgets to the 70.92- and 69.26-minute paths before rerunning them.
meta_reflection: The 40% estimate is conditional: placing the 69.26-minute run entirely beneath the 70.92-minute run would subtract 69.26 minutes from 172.5 minutes if the jobs are independent and device-separable. Independence is not recorded, so only future queue and telemetry receipts can convert this scheduling bound into measured savings.
